It also, among other things, would increase the number of beds that must be added or removed at a health care facility in order to trigger a certificate of need. It would also require the Comprehensive Homicide Elimination Strategy Task Force to submit to the Council a report on the District’s programs and policies for witness protection and assistance.

B26-0028.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced Bill 26-28 would prohibit segregated confinement in jails and limit the use of safe cells. It would require that incarcerated people with mental health emergencies receive the care to which they are entitled. The Department of Corrections is required to create a plan to eliminate segregated confinement and report to the Council the impacts of doing so.
B26-0028.last_action: Referred to Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety
B26-0028.location_name: Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety
B26-0028.title: Eliminating Restrictive and Segregated Enclosures (“ERASE”) Solitary Confinement Act of 2025

B26-0029.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced Bill 26-29 would assist survivors of sexual misconduct by requiring institutions of higher education in the District to retain a confidential resource advisor (CRA) to provide emergency and ongoing support to reporting parties at institutions of higher education. It would require amnesty protections for reporting parties of sexual misconduct in certain cases. Institutions would be required to facilitate mandatory annual sexual misconduct trainings for all students and personnel. It would establish minimum criteria for institutions’ sexual misconduct policies. It would also, among other things, require institutions to submit to the Higher Education Licensure Commission a report containing data about sexual misconduct on campus. FISCAL NOTE - This bill is Subject to Appropriations. Please see the Fiscal Impact Statement for more information.
B26-0029.last_action: Law L26-0101, Effective from Mar 19, 2026 Published in DC Register Vol 73 and Page 005735
B26-0029.title: Institution of Higher Education Sexual Misconduct Reporting and Resource Accessibility Act of 2025

It does this by requiring persons who file with the federal government what is called a Hart-Scott-Rodino form and related documents (“HSR documents”) to file them with the Office of the Attorney General. It also provides civil penalties for noncompliance.

B26-0030.location_name: Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety
B26-0030.title: Uniform Antitrust Pre-Merger Notification Act of 2025

B26-0051.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced Bill 26-51 would establish the Alcoholic Beverage and Cannabis Board and the Alcoholic Beverage and Cannabis Administration. It would also establish a Cannabis Regulation Division and a Cannabis Advisory Committee. It would prohibit the sale of cannabis or cannabis products without a license and prohibit exchanges of cannabis for purchasing another item. It also establishes guidelines for Social Equity Applicants and a Community Reinvestment Fund, Program and Board, among other things.
B26-0051.last_action: Re-Referred to Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety, and Committee of the Whole
B26-0051.location_name: Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety, Committee on Business and Economic Development, and Committee of the Whole
B26-0051.title: Comprehensive Cannabis Legalization and Regulation Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0052.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced Bill 26-52 would establish a Group Violence Intervention Initiative and an organizational structure to guide the efforts of the Initiative. It would allow the Metropolitan Police Department to hire civilian personnel to respond to and investigate certain property crimes and cold cases. The Sentencing Commission is required to publish a biannual report on repeat violent offenders in the District and authorizes the Mayor to take corrective actions to remediate criminal blight at properties in the District. It would require the Director of the Department of Healthcare Finance to submit an amendment to the Medicaid state plan to make community violence prevention services available to Medicaid beneficiaries.
B26-0052.last_action: Public Hearing on B26-0052 View Public Hearing Record
B26-0052.location_name: Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety with comments from the Committee on Health
B26-0052.title: Evidence-Based Gun Violence Reduction and Prevention Act of 2025

Please see Fiscal Impact Statement and the CFO Funding Certification letter for more information.

B26-0053.location_name: Committee of the Whole with comments from the Committee on Executive Administration and Labor
B26-0053.title: Vacant to Vibrant to Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0063.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-63 would give a disabled child with an individualized education program the right to remain in their initial placement feeder pattern unless there is no program available in their feeder pattern. It would require that an LEA consult with the IEP team of a child with a disability prior to any change in the child’s service location. It would require a written explanation to the parent of a child with a disability before any change in service location. B26-0092.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-92 would require that all lead service lines in the District on both public and private property be replaced with non-lead lines by December 31, 2030 and prohibit the practice of partial lead service line replacements. Under this bill, the installation of new lead, brass, or galvanized steel service lines would be prohibited. It would also require that owners of private property serviced by a lead service line enroll in the Lead Service Line Replacement Program or replace the lead service line themselves. It prescribe how DC Water is to treat and test properties with service lines of unknown composition and also provide lead service line replacements at District properties at no cost to the property owner. It would establish a high-priority lead service line replacement program to prioritize replacement of lead service lines at child development facilities, multi-unit residential properties, properties that previously underwent a partial lead service line replacement, and homes with emergency service line repairs. DC Water is required to maintain a service line inventory and provide water filtration devices and replacement cartridges to all properties serviced by a service line made of lead or of unknown composition until at least 6 months after the property’s lead service line is replaced. As a condition of a real property sale or transfer, a purchaser must enroll in the Lead Service Line Replacement Program or replace the lead service line. Among other things, it would prescribe certain rights and protections for occupants residing at a property serviced by a lead service line. It would also require that the Department of Energy and Environment engage community-based organizations (“CBO”) to review contractor lead service line replacements and to set deadlines for residents to comply with the requirements of this act. The Mayor is required to issue regulations to implement this act. It amends the Fiscal Year 2005 Budget Support Act of 2004 to remove language establishing the Lead Pipe Replacement Assistance Program.
B26-0092.last_action: Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0092 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0092.location_name: Committee on Transportation and the Environment
B26-0092.title: Lead-Free DC Omnibus Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0174.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-174 would enhance consumer protections by providing enhanced remedies to secure compliance, authorize fines, costs and fees for failure to fully comply with an investigative subpoena regarding a consumer protection case. It grants additional consumer protection enforcement authority to the Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection. It would prohibit retaliation for consumer complaints and aiding and abetting prohibited trade practices. It would authorize asset freezes as injunctive relief and set mandatory minimum penalties for violations and allow for the recovery of legal costs in actions involving the Attorney General. It would authorize the use of interrogatories in investigations. It would specify that service may be made by any method reasonably calculated to give actual notice. It would allow use of sworn investigative statements for perjury prosecutions and allow the Mayor and the Office of the Attorney General to issue rules. FISCAL NOTE - This bill was passed Subject to Appropriations. Bill fully funded via Act 26-416. Please see Fiscal Impact Statement and Funding Certification Letter for more information.

B26-0174.title: Enhancing Consumer Protection Procedures Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0202.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-202 would establish an Office of Social Housing Developments to administer the construction, maintenance, and growth of District-owned residential properties designed to be mixed-income housing with not less than two-thirds of a building developed as family units and not less than two-thirds of units rented as permanently affordable units for low income households. It would establish a framework for tenant governance, environmentally conscious building standards, and street-level amenities at social housing developments. It would also allow investments in District-owned social housing developments and authorize the sale of certain real estate in the District of Columbia no longer required for public purposes. It would require that the Mayor evaluate such properties for conversion into social housing developments before disposing of them among other things.

B26-0314.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-314, the Local News Funding Act of 2025 would create a system where residents decide which news outlets receive public grants through "news coupons." Each registered voter receives five news coupons through a secure online system that can be allocated to any news outlet registered with a new Community Journalism Board. Each coupon represents a fraction of the total grant funding available. If more residents allocate coupons to a particular outlet, that outlet receives a larger share of the funding.

B26-0369.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-369 would clarify that the ABC Board may limit a licensee’s hours of operation and permitted hours for an entertainment endorsement, summer garden, and sidewalk café. The bill also establishes a separate fine schedule for noise violations and allows the ABC Board to suspend a liquor license and place restrictions on certain licensee endorsements following a fourth or subsequent noise violation within a two-year period.

It would transfer screened-out educational neglect referrals from Child and Family Services Agency to the Department of Human Services for follow up and support resources. It would also require the Mayor to propose a unified referral system for educational neglect and truancy by March 31, 2028.

DPR would provide approved vendors a grant between $8,000 to $12,000 to operate and sell food and beverages between April 1st and October 31st at recreation centers, parks, and other DPR facilities in all eight wards.
B26-0475.last_action: Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0475 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0475.title: Park Concessions Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0476.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-476 would exempt 100 percent of the taxation of real property, including the joint real property of married individuals and serving spouses of disabled veterans or veterans who died in active duty.
B26-0476.location_name: Committee on Business and Economic Development
B26-0476.title: Disabled Veterans Complete Property Tax Exemption Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0477.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-477 would require housing providers to accept a reusable tenant screening report from prospective tenants in lieu of conducting a new tenant screening and among other things, to require a housing provider to furnish a prospective tenant with a dated copy of their tenant screening report.
B26-0477.title: Portable Tenant Screening Report Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0478.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-478 would decouple the homeowner property tax credit from the renter tax credit, creating a separate Renter Tax Credit. It would amend the cap for claimants of the Renter Tax Credit and expand the Renter Tax Credit to provide support to unhoused individuals and individuals in temporary housing who may lack fixed rents. It also allows Renter Tax Credit claimants whose credit exceeds $1,200 to elect for monthly instead of annual payment.
B26-0478.location_name: Committee on Business and Economic Development with comments from the Committee on Housing
B26-0478.title: Renter Tax Credit Expansion Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0479.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-479 would establish a grant program within the Child and Family Services Agency to support the creation and operation of Youth Villages across the District of Columbia. It would also provide grant funding to nonprofit organizations to develop neighborhood-based, intergenerational networks to provide daily supports to youth up to age 25.
B26-0479.title: Youth Villages Grant Establishment Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0480.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-480 would codify the ability of residents at Department of Corrections facilities to testify before the Council of the District of Columbia. It would provide access to Advisory Neighborhood Commissioners and internet services for the purpose of engaging in the legislative process and participate in hearings. The Department of Corrections is required to provide materials explaining the legislative process and must submit an annual report to the Council and Mayor.
B26-0480.last_action: Public Hearing on B26-0480 View Public Hearing Record
B26-0480.location_name: Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety
B26-0480.title: Ensuring Access and Supporting Engagement (EASE) for DOC residents Act of 2025

B26-0481.digest: bill summary - As introduced, Bill 26-481 would require the Department of Parks and Recreation to establish and operate a minimum of four comprehensive teen centers; and also require the creation of Youth Advisory Councils for each center to ensure youth participation in governance, programming, and operations.
B26-0481.last_action: Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0481 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0481.title: Teen Center Establishment Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0482.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-482 would direct the Deputy Mayor for Education to contract with a third-party contractor to develop a smartphone application that directly connects youth and young adults in the District to flexible, paid work opportunities in the private sector.
B26-0482.last_action: Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0482 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0482.title: DC Youth Links App Act of 2025

B26-0483.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-483 would establish a home trash shed incentive program for the safe storage of trash receptacles. It would require replacing public trash cans that are in disrepair with better-sealed, censored trash cans. It would also revive the Trash Compactor Tax Incentive Amendment Act of 2014.
B26-0483.last_action: Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0483 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0483.location_name: Committee on Public Works and Operations
B26-0483.title: Rodent Abatement Through Smart Solutions (RATSS) Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0484.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-484 would eliminate the rule that prohibits the Real Property Tax Appeals Commission (“RPTAC”) from adjusting a property’s estimated market value if the Office of Tax and Revenue’s (“OTR’s”) assessment was within 5%. It would also require all RPTAC appeals decisions from the previous years be decided within 30 days and would extend the deadline by which such decisions need to be decided. Additionally, it would allow a letter of authorization to remain in effect for up to 3 years and throughout multiple levels of appeals, standardize appeals filing deadlines to business days instead of standard days, and allow property owners to opt in to electronic delivery of OTR appeals decisions.
B26-0484.last_action: Public Hearing on B26-0484 View Public Hearing Record
B26-0484.location_name: Committee on Business and Economic Development
B26-0484.title: Fairness and Accuracy in Real Property Tax Assessments Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0485.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-485 would ensure that art galleries exempt from property tax may also exempt space used for business purposes that support the cultural mission of the organization.
B26-0485.last_action: Re-Referred to Committee of the Whole
B26-0485.location_name: Committee on Business and Economic Development
B26-0485.title: Art Gallery Tax Exemption Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0486.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-486 would include elective oocyte retrieval and oocyte cryopreservation in the list of fertility treatments required to be covered by health insurance in the District of Columbia.
B26-0486.location_name: Committee on Health, and Committee on Business and Economic Development
B26-0486.title: Expanding Fertility Treatment Options Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0487.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-487 allows businesses to apply for a tax credit if between 2027 and 2032 they create at least 25 new jobs for District residents. The bill requires that the positions be paid at least the average yearly wage in DC. Businesses must retain the new positions for at least one year.
B26-0487.last_action: Re-Referred to Committee of the Whole
B26-0487.location_name: Committee on Business and Economic Development
B26-0487.title: Job Growth Incentive Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0488.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-488 would establish the Pathways to Prosperity Program to provide zero-interest forgivable loans for tuition and living expenses. It would establish a non-lapsing fund to support the program and also establish eligibility criteria and conditions of participation.
B26-0488.title: Apprenticeships and Credentials as Pathways to Prosperity Act of 2025

B26-0489.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-489 would revise prioritization metrics and data collection reporting requirements imposed on education agencies.
B26-0489.last_action: Public Hearing on B26-0489 View Public Hearing Record
B26-0489.title: PACE Clarification Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0490.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-490 would prohibit the District of Columbia Public Library from entering into or renewing licensing agreements with publishers of electronic literary materials that restrict District residents’ access to books.
B26-0490.last_action: Law L26-0149, Effective from Jul 18, 2026 Published in DC Register Vol 73 and Page 011057
B26-0490.title: Library E-book Pricing Fairness Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0491.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-491 would direct local education agencies to adopt and implement a model AI literacy policy addressing appropriate use and instruction of artificial and generative intelligence by students and staff for educational purposes.
B26-0491.last_action: Referred to Committee of the Whole
B26-0491.title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy in Education Act of 2025

B26-0492.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-492 would require the Department of Health to require the development of a rodent abatement dashboard and report on rodent abatement efforts. It would also require the Department of Public Works provide notice to Advisory Neighborhood Commissions before the removal of public trash cans in residential zones and require that sightings of active rodent or vector activity during enforcement activities be referred to the Department of Health.
B26-0492.last_action: Public Hearing on B26-0492 View Public Hearing Record
B26-0492.location_name: Committee on Health, and Committee on Public Works and Operations
B26-0492.title: Rodent Abatement and Transparency (RAT) Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0493.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-493 would clarify grounds, notice, and procedures for receiverships. It would also establish cost recovery and lien mechanisms, as well as authorize tenant protections. It would permit dissolution and related remedies in cases of fraud or abuse, and for other purposes.
B26-0493.location_name: Committee on Business and Economic Development, and Committee of the Whole
B26-0493.title: Strengthening Tenant Receivership and Oversight for Neighborhood Growth (STRONG) Homes Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0494.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-494 would revise the eligibility requirements for accountancy licensure by authorizing a holder of a baccalaureate degree with two years of experience and who has passed an examination in accounting and auditing to obtain a license. It would also amend the mobility requirements for those who are licensed in another jurisdiction and want to practice in the District.
B26-0494.last_action: Law Number L26-0183 Effective from Sep 25, 2026
B26-0494.location_name: Committee on Public Works and Operations with comments from the Committee on Business and Economic Development
B26-0494.title: Accountancy Practice Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0495.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-495 would clarify the minimum required coverages for condominium owners in the District. It would also increase the deductible responsibility for individual condominium owners.
B26-0495.title: Condominium Insurance Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0523.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-523 would require the Department of Health Care Finance to develop a single application process for providers seeking to be credentialed or recredentialed with a managed care organization. It would set timeframes and notice requirements for the Department of Health Care Finance to respond to applications. FISCAL NOTE - This bill is Subject to Appropriations. Please see the Fiscal Impact Statement for more information.
B26-0523.last_action: Committee Mark-up of B26-0523 by the Health Committee
B26-0523.title: Streamlining Medicaid Credentialing Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0524.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-524 would create a new misdemeanor criminal offense and a new felony criminal offense for nonconsensual distribution of sexually explicit images, video, or audio of an individual created or altered through use of digital technology, including the use of artificial intelligence.
B26-0524.last_action: Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0524 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0524.location_name: Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety
B26-0524.title: Distribution of False Sexual Imagery Prohibition Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0525.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-525 would prohibit geofencing around facilities that provide health services, preventing the tracking or targeting of individuals based on their location. It would require controllers (the entities that determine how and why personal health data is used) to publish clear, accessible privacy policies describing what data is collected, how it is used, and with whom it is shared. It would also mandate consent before any collection, processing, or disclosure of personal health data, and allows individuals to withdraw consent at any time. It would also create a right to deletion.
B26-0525.title: Personal Health Data Security Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0526.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-526 would mandate that the Department of Corrections (DOC) evaluate students for special education services who were not evaluated before entering DOC custody. DOC must provide education services for current Individualized Education Program (IEP) holders in their custody. It, among other things, would also require that DOC establish and maintain in a publicly accessible and searchable online tracking system for resident service requests and complaints. FISCAL NOTE - Sections 2 and 3 are passed Subject to Appropriations. Please see the Fiscal Impact Statement for more information.
B26-0526.last_action: Law Number L26-0188 Effective from Oct 02, 2026
B26-0526.location_name: Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety with comments from the Committee of the Whole
B26-0526.title: Leading Education Access for Reentry and Necessary Success (LEARNS) Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0531.title: Urban Agriculture Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0541.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-541 would establish energy efficiency and electrification requirements for new construction projects receiving assistance from the Housing Production Trust Fund. It would require periodic reporting on the development of universal net zero energy building code regulations that will apply to residential and mixed-use construction. It would also limit certain net zero energy compliance provisions and add a requirement for adding renewable energy systems when half of more of a rooftop is being replaced for residential projects.
B26-0541.location_name: Committee on Housing, and Committee on Transportation and the Environment
B26-0541.title: Green Housing Coordination Amendment Act of 2025

B26-0542.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-542 would require that DHCD offer administrative assistance to affordable housing development projects to promote prompt attention from utility partners in the permitting process. It would require DHCD to make technical expert consultants available to these same projects to reduce how often utility connection design issues catch developers off guard. DHCD staff would also spearhead a coordinated effort between government agencies and utilities to integrate the utilities’ permitting updates into existing government data systems for tracking permit issues. B26-0769.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-769 would authorize the Mayor to enter into a public-private financing agreement with DC United to redevelop Audi Field through the installation of a climate-controlling roof. It would create a public private financing model that would include contributions from the stadium and the District to realize over one hundred new events annually. It would establish a Soccer Stadium Preservation and Improvement Fund and among other things Provide tax exemptions on excess soccer stadium site revenue. The real property tax rate for Class 1C properties is set at $2.50 per $100 of assessed value.

B26-0803.digest: BILL SUMMARY - Under the Uniform act, a financially distressed business, an assignor, may transfer control of its assets to an assignee, who acts as a fiduciary for the business’ creditors. The assignee may sell the business’ assets and distribute the proceeds to the business’ creditors. These proceeds go towards payment of the creditors’ claims against the assignor. The Act creates an alternative to other procedures available to the assignor for winding up its business, and provides benefits that are not available through a federal bankruptcy case or a receivership.
B26-0803.last_action: Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0803 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0803.location_name: Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety
B26-0803.title: Uniform Assignment for Benefit of Creditors Act of 2026

It requires the licensing of dispatch service providers to provide services to individuals with disabilities and also establish standards for wheelchair accessible vehicles. It would establish procedures for operator background checks and driving history checks and define fare structures applicable to for-hire passenger service. Among other things, IT would prohibit surveillance-based fare discrimination.

B26-0818.title: For-Hire Passenger Service Reform Act of 2026

B26-0830.title: Vacated Rates Clarification Amendment Act of 2026

B26-0831.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-831 would allow the Office of Advisory Neighborhood Commissions to evaluate any proposal to establish single-member districts to ensure the neighborhood cohesiveness and viability of such districts. The OANC would submit a report to the Council on its findings and recommendations. It would require that the Council consider the report of the OANC when making adjustments in the boundaries of the Advisory Neighborhood Commission single-member districts and ANC areas. It would also establish requirements for certain ANC seats to be considered vacant. It establishes in person voting procedures for the Department of Corrections with the assistance of the Board of Elections. It clarifies that no Commission may solicit donations unless specifically authorized. Among other things, it provides that a copy of each Commission’s by laws and all amendments thereto shall not be effective until transmitted to the Council and the OANC. It also establishes procedures for the release of ANC allotment funding over a certain amount.
B26-0831.title: Advisory Neighborhood Commissions Functions Modernization Amendment Act of 2026

B26-0832.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-832 would authorize Advisory Neighborhood Commissions to expend funds through certain third-party digital payment platforms.

B26-0833.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-833 would modernize the District’s EMS system by creating a Board of Emergency Medical Services to regulate EMS personnel. It would grant subpoena authority to the Mayor and the Mayor’s delegates. It would update licensure requirements and scopes of practice by establishing a Certified Community Health Worker license under the Board of Social Work. It would create a temporary waiver process for certain foreign-licensed health professionals. It repeals the requirement that the Council review Massage Therapy regulations. It would also modernize criminal background check requirements.
B26-0833.last_action: Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0833 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0833.location_name: Committee on Health with comments from the Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety
B26-0833.title: Health Occupations and Emergency Medical Services Amendment Act of 2026

B26-0853.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-853 would prohibit health insurers from automatically downcoding a claim using artificial intelligence based solely on the reported diagnosis code. An insurer changing a service code submitted by a clinician to a lower-level code, can result in lower reimbursement. It requires they notify the clinician to clearly indicate the claim was downcoded. It provides clinicians with a process for appealing downcoded claims. It makes violations of this act enforceable by the Department of Health and Human Services.
B26-0853.last_action: Notice of Intent to Act on B26-0853 Published in the District of Columbia Register
B26-0853.title: Transparency in Downcoding Amendment Act of 2026

B26-0856.digest: BILL SUMMARY - As introduced, Bill 26-856 would require student identification cards issued under the Student Identification Card Act of 2025 to be included free of charge and include all the functionality of a District of Columbia Public Library card. It would also enable access to Department of Parks and Recreation facilities, convey how to contact the national Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and be provided free of charge.

B26-0856.title: Expanding Access for Student Identification Empowers Readers (EASIER) Act of 2026
